title: 1977 BMW 320i with Just 9000 Miles For Sale on Bring a Trailer
summary: Most owners drove the snot out of these cars, but somehow this one was preserved.
whatHappening: A remarkably preserved 1977 BMW 320i with just 9,000 original miles is currently listed for sale on Bring a Trailer, the online classic car auction platform. The low mileage is exceptionally rare for a car of this age, as most examples from that era were driven heavily by their owners.
whoInvolved: Bring a Trailer, a Hearst-owned automotive auction website specializing in classic cars, is hosting the sale. BMW, the German automaker, manufactured the 3 Series line beginning in 1975, with the 320i representing one of the early models in what would become the company's most successful compact executive car platform.
whyMatters: Ultra-low-mileage vintage vehicles command premium prices and represent time capsules of automotive engineering and design from their era. This particular car's preservation offers collectors and enthusiasts a rare opportunity to own a 1977 BMW 3 Series in what appears to be near-original condition, reflecting both the craftsmanship of that generation and the rarity of cars that escaped heavy daily use.
articleBody:
A 1977 BMW 320i showing just 9,000 miles on the odometer has appeared on Bring a Trailer, the online auction platform for classic vehicles. The car represents an extraordinary find in the collector car market, where examples from the late 1970s are typically worn from decades of regular driving and use.

BMW introduced the 3 Series in May 1975 as the successor to the 02 series, establishing what would become one of the automotive industry's most durable and beloved compact executive car lines. The early models, including this 1977 320i, are prized by enthusiasts for their mechanical simplicity and driving characteristics. However, according to Car and Driver, most owners drove the snot out of these cars during their working lives, making survivors with minimal mileage exceptionally scarce.

The 320i variant of that era represented BMW's entry-level offering in the 3 Series, powered by a fuel-injected four-cylinder engine. The model struck a balance between performance, economy, and affordability that made it popular among European and American drivers. What sets this particular example apart is the apparent dedication of its original owner or subsequent caretakers to preserve it rather than use it as transportation.

Vehicles with such low mileage typically command significant premiums at auction, as they offer collectors the chance to experience a car much as it would have been when new. Paint condition, interior preservation, and the integrity of mechanical systems all remain largely uncompromised by the wear that accumulated mileage would bring. Bring a Trailer, acquired by Hearst in 2020, has become a prominent marketplace for such finds, attracting serious collectors and enthusiasts worldwide.

The sale of this 320i underscores the enduring appeal of early BMW 3 Series automobiles. Whether purchased for restoration, collection, or as a genuine-article example of late-1970s BMW engineering, the car represents a snapshot of an important era in automotive history when German precision manufacturing began establishing global market dominance.

title: Wild Horses: Roush Mustang vs. P-51 Mustang Fighter Plane
summary: In which we contrive one more comparo dedicated to playing with another person's excellent toys, thereby gaining entrance to horse heaven.
whatHappening: Car and Driver is running a comparison test between a high-performance Roush Mustang sports car and a North American P-51 Mustang fighter plane—two machines that share a name but occupy vastly different worlds. The publication frames the piece as an indulgent exercise in getting behind the wheel and controls of someone else's exceptional vehicles.
whoInvolved: Roush Performance, the American high-performance automotive company founded by Jack Roush in 1995, is represented through its modified Mustang sports car. The P-51 Mustang is a legendary World War II-era fighter aircraft designed by North American Aviation in 1940, originally created in response to a British request for long-range fighter capability.
whyMatters: The comparison highlights the enduring appeal of the Mustang nameplate across different eras and mediums—from mid-century military aviation to modern performance automotive engineering. Such juxtapositions capture the imagination of enthusiasts and casual readers alike, celebrating American engineering achievement across generations.
articleBody:
The Mustang name evokes different things depending on context: for car enthusiasts, it conjures images of sleek, powerful machines built for speed on pavement; for aviation historians, it recalls one of World War II's most iconic fighter aircraft. Car and Driver's latest comparison brings both worlds together in a playful exploration that treats the comparison as much about accessing extraordinary machinery as it is about the vehicles themselves.

Roush Performance has built its reputation since 1995 on engineering and manufacturing high-performance components that transform street cars and competitive racing machines. The company, operated by automotive mogul Jack Roush, takes the Ford Mustang platform and elevates it into a serious performance vehicle capable of impressing even seasoned gearheads. By contrast, the P-51 Mustang represents an earlier era of American engineering ambition—a fighter-bomber designed in 1940 by a North American Aviation team led by James H. Kindelberger. What began as a response to the British Purchasing Commission's request for fighters became one of the most celebrated military aircraft ever built, seeing service not only in World War II but also in the Korean War and beyond.

According to Car and Driver, the comparison is framed tongue-in-cheek as an excuse to play with extraordinary machines that most people will never access, turning the exercise into a tour of what the publication calls "horse heaven." The piece captures something fundamental about American automotive and aviation culture: a love affair with speed, performance, and the machines that deliver it.

The comparison underscores how the Mustang name has anchored itself across different technological frontiers. The original P-51 represented cutting-edge design for its time—a long-range, single-seat fighter that pushed the boundaries of what aircraft could accomplish. The modern Roush Mustang, meanwhile, represents contemporary automotive performance engineering, applying decades of racing and development expertise to consumer-available horsepower. Both machines, in their respective domains, embody the pursuit of speed and capability.

title: 2001 Roush Stage 3 Mustang Test: Cobra Killer
summary: The race-car builder finally turns out a supercharged Mustang that can run with a Corvette Z06. You will need to bring money.
whatHappening: Roush Performance has engineered a supercharged 2001 Mustang that finally delivers genuine high-performance credentials, capable of competing with the Corvette Z06. The achievement marks a significant moment for the race-car builder's street-car division.
whoInvolved: Roush Performance is an American automotive company founded in 1995 by automotive mogul Jack Roush, specializing in high-performance components for both racing and street applications. The Ford Mustang, manufactured since 1964, is America's longest-running nameplate in continuous production and the namesake of the entire "pony car" segment.
whyMatters: This supercharged Mustang demonstrates that affordable American performance cars can now challenge exotic competitors like the Corvette Z06, potentially shifting buyer expectations in the performance segment. For Roush Performance, it validates their engineering expertise in translating race-car technology to consumer vehicles, opening new market opportunities for premium Mustang modifications.
articleBody:
Roush Performance has completed a significant engineering feat: transforming the 2001 Ford Mustang into a legitimate high-performance contender through supercharger technology. The Stage 3 variant represents the company's most ambitious street-car project to date, capable of running with Chevrolet's vaunted Corvette Z06, a car that commands significantly higher pricing.

For a company primarily known for race-car engineering, Roush Performance's foray into accessible performance modifications reflects broader market opportunity. The Ford Mustang, which has been in continuous production since 1964 and remains one of Ford's best-selling nameplates, provides an ideal platform for performance upgrades. The long-hood, short-deck proportions that defined the original pony car continue to dominate the Mustang's design language, and Roush's engineers have leveraged these proportions with their supercharger installation.

According to Car and Driver, the financial investment required to acquire this Stage 3 Mustang is substantial, positioning it as a premium modification option rather than a budget performance upgrade. The supercharger setup delivers output levels previously unreachable in naturally aspirated Mustang platforms, allowing street drivers genuine competitive parity with mid-range exotic performance vehicles.

The engineering challenge centered on packaging a supercharging system within the Mustang's engine bay without compromising reliability or serviceability. Roush's race-car background provided crucial expertise in high-boost applications, thermal management, and internal engine reinforcement—knowledge typically confined to competitive motorsports applications.

This project holds significance beyond a single performance vehicle. It demonstrates that American manufacturers and their specialist partners can deliver supercar-adjacent performance through targeted modification, potentially democratizing access to genuine performance credentials. The Stage 3 Mustang proves that commitment to engineering excellence transcends the divide between full-time racing operations and street-car customization.

title: View Photos of the Roush Mustang vs P-51 Mustang Fighter Plane
summary: See the interior and exterior of the 1999 Roush Mustang and P-51 Mustang Fighter Plane from every angle.
whatHappening: Car and Driver is offering a detailed photo gallery comparing the 1999 Roush Mustang performance car with the North American P-51 Mustang fighter aircraft, showcasing both vehicles from multiple interior and exterior angles.
whoInvolved: Roush Performance, the American high-performance automotive company founded in 1995 by Jack Roush, engineered the modified Mustang. The P-51 Mustang is a legendary World War II-era fighter aircraft designed by North American Aviation in 1940 and used extensively in combat operations.
whyMatters: The comparison highlights the evolution of American engineering and design across different eras—from military aviation to street performance vehicles. Such visual juxtapositions offer enthusiasts and historians a tangible way to appreciate the shared design legacy and performance heritage between iconic machines separated by decades.
articleBody:
Car and Driver has assembled a comprehensive photographic comparison between two American icons bearing the same name: the 1999 Roush Mustang and the North American P-51 Mustang fighter plane. The gallery presents both vehicles from every angle, allowing viewers to examine the styling, construction, and engineering of these distinctly different machines side by side.

The Roush Mustang represents the pinnacle of 1990s automotive performance modification. Roush Performance, founded in 1995 by automotive mogul Jack Roush, specializes in engineering and manufacturing high-performance components for both street cars and competitive racing applications. The 1999 model showcased in the photos demonstrates the company's expertise in enhancing the classic Mustang platform with contemporary performance enhancements and refinements.

The P-51 Mustang, by contrast, belongs to an entirely different era of American engineering. Designed in 1940 by a team at North American Aviation headed by James H. Kindelberger, the P-51 became an American long-range, single-seat fighter and fighter-bomber during World War II and the Korean War. The aircraft was originally conceived in response to a request from the British Purchasing Commission, which had approached North American Aviation about building Curtiss P-40 fighters under license. Rather than manufacture an outdated design, North American Aviation created an entirely new fighter that would become one of the most celebrated military aircraft of its generation.

According to Car and Driver, the photographic comparison reveals the distinct philosophies behind each machine's design. The Roush Mustang displays the aggressive aerodynamic touches and muscular proportions characteristic of late-1990s performance vehicles, while the P-51's elliptical fuselage and laminar-flow wing represent the aeronautical innovations of the World War II era. Examining both vehicles side by side illustrates how design language and engineering priorities have evolved across the decades.

Both vehicles share more than just a name—they represent American ingenuity applied to performance and speed. While separated by more than half a century, the Roush Mustang and the P-51 Mustang each embodied the cutting-edge technology and design sensibilities of their respective time periods. The photo gallery provides enthusiasts and automotive historians with a unique visual document of this shared legacy.

title: 2008 Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren Roadster on Bring a Trailer
summary: The road-car collaboration between Mercedes-Benz and McLaren followed from their F1 tie-up.
whatHappening: A 2008 Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren Roadster is being offered for sale on Bring a Trailer, the online auction platform. This rare supercar represents one of the most exclusive collaborations in automotive history.
whoInvolved: Mercedes-Benz and McLaren, two legendary automotive manufacturers whose partnership extended from their dominant Formula 1 racing alliance into road-car production. The SLR McLaren was the physical embodiment of this high-performance collaboration between the German luxury brand and the British racing specialist.
whyMatters: The SLR McLaren remains a significant milestone in supercar history, symbolizing what happens when two world-class engineering teams combine resources and expertise. As these limited-production vehicles become increasingly collectible, their auction sales reflect the enduring appeal of early-2000s hypercar design and the prestige of Mercedes-McLaren partnership vehicles.
articleBody:
A 2008 Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren Roadster is finding its way to auction on Bring a Trailer, offering enthusiasts a rare opportunity to acquire one of the most exclusive supercars ever produced. The roadster variant of the SLR McLaren represents the pinnacle of the Mercedes-McLaren collaboration, combining German engineering refinement with British racing pedigree.

The SLR McLaren was born from the storied partnership between Mercedes-Benz and McLaren that defined Formula 1 racing in the late 1980s and early 1990s. When the two companies decided to channel their motorsport expertise into a road-going supercar, the result was a vehicle that pushed the boundaries of performance, luxury, and exclusivity. According to Car and Driver, the road-car collaboration between Mercedes-Benz and McLaren followed from their F1 tie-up, bringing decades of combined racing knowledge to a civilian automobile.

The SLR McLaren Roadster variant took the already-exclusive coupe and enhanced it with the added drama of an open-air driving experience. With a carbon-fiber body, a hand-assembled engine, and technology derived directly from Formula 1 development, the Roadster represented the absolute apex of early-2000s supercar engineering. The removable hard top and retractable wind deflector allowed drivers to experience the full sensory assault of the vehicle's performance while maintaining practical usability.

As the collector car market has matured over the past two decades, vehicles like the SLR McLaren Roadster have become increasingly sought-after. The limited production numbers, combined with the historical significance of the Mercedes-McLaren partnership, have made these cars objects of desire for serious collectors. Each sale through platforms like Bring a Trailer provides a benchmark for the market value of these exclusive machines.

For potential buyers, the appearance of a 2008 SLR McLaren Roadster at auction represents more than just the opportunity to acquire a high-performance vehicle. It reflects a particular moment in automotive history when two manufacturing giants combined their resources to create something unprecedented. The sale serves as a testament to the enduring appeal of supercar design from that era and the prestige that continues to surround the Mercedes-McLaren nameplate.

title: Genesis Confirms That the Upcoming GV90 Will Have Coach Doors

whatHappening: Genesis has confirmed that its upcoming GV90 luxury SUV will feature coach doors, a distinctive design element inspired by the 2024 Neolun concept vehicle. The vehicle is set to be officially revealed in August.
whoInvolved: Genesis, the luxury vehicle division of Hyundai Motor Group, is behind the GV90's development and design direction. The company has drawn inspiration from its Neolun concept car in shaping this new flagship SUV.
whyMatters: Coach doors represent a premium design choice that signals Genesis's ambition to position the GV90 as a high-end, statement vehicle in the luxury SUV segment. This decision reflects the brand's commitment to distinctive styling that differentiates it from competitors and appeals to affluent buyers seeking exclusivity and innovation.
articleBody:
Genesis has officially confirmed that the upcoming GV90 will feature coach doors, a luxury design element that underscores the brand's positioning of the vehicle as a flagship model. According to Car and Driver, the GV90's design direction draws inspiration from the 2024 Neolun concept car, which previewed the styling direction for Genesis's new generation of vehicles. The model is slated to be revealed to the public in August, marking a significant moment for the luxury automaker.

Coach doors—doors that open in the reverse direction of conventional doors, typically found on only the most exclusive vehicles—represent a bold design choice. The feature has historically been associated with ultra-premium automobiles and signals a shift toward more distinctive, sculptural design language. By incorporating this element into the GV90, Genesis is making a clear statement about the vehicle's position within its lineup and its appeal to discerning luxury buyers.

The Neolun concept served as a design and technological showcase for Genesis's vision of future luxury vehicles. Its influence on the GV90 suggests that the production model will carry forward the concept's emphasis on innovative styling, premium materials, and sophisticated proportions. This design continuity between concept and production vehicle is intentional, allowing Genesis to translate aspirational design language into an accessible luxury product.

The GV90 arrives as Genesis continues to expand its SUV portfolio and strengthen its presence in the competitive luxury segment. The brand has been pursuing a strategy of distinctive design and technological innovation to differentiate itself from established luxury marques. The addition of coach doors to the GV90 fits squarely within this approach, offering buyers a visible symbol of the vehicle's premium status and the brand's commitment to design excellence.

With the August reveal date approaching, automotive enthusiasts and luxury buyers will soon see the full extent of how Genesis has translated the Neolun concept into a production-ready vehicle. The confirmation of coach doors provides early insight into the design direction, signaling that Genesis is not shying away from bold, distinctive features that set its vehicles apart in the marketplace.

whatHappening: Ford's CEO is warning employees that Chinese automakers will likely enter the U.S. market within the next 5-10 years despite current trade barriers. The executive is signaling that the arrival of Chinese competitors is inevitable, even if it takes longer than in other markets.
whoInvolved: Ford Motor Company, one of Detroit's Big Three automakers, is being led by a CEO who is publicly acknowledging competitive threats from Chinese manufacturers. Chinese automakers, including BYD and others, have dominated their home market and are aggressively expanding internationally.
whyMatters: Chinese automakers entering the U.S. market would fundamentally reshape the automotive industry and intensify competition for domestic manufacturers already facing margin pressures. This could accelerate innovation in electric vehicles and force U.S. automakers to improve pricing and efficiency to remain competitive. For consumers, it could mean more vehicle choices and potentially lower prices.
moreContext: Chinese automakers have become the world's largest EV producers and have rapidly gained market share in Asia, Europe, and other regions. Currently, U.S. tariffs and trade restrictions effectively block Chinese vehicles from the American market, but Ford's warning suggests these barriers may eventually fall or be circumvented. BYD is now the global leader in vehicle sales when including EVs and plug-in hybrids. Ford's public acknowledgment reflects broader industry concerns about how trade policy and tariff changes could reshape the competitive landscape.

whoInvolved: Mercedes-Benz, the German luxury automaker, is initiating the recall. The company is one of the world's largest premium vehicle manufacturers and has faced increased scrutiny from regulators over safety defects in recent years.
whyMatters: A rolling-away defect poses serious safety risks to owners, parked vehicles nearby, and pedestrians in the vicinity. This recall could result in significant warranty costs for Mercedes-Benz and may damage consumer confidence in the brand's quality and reliability during a competitive period for luxury automakers.
moreContext: Rolling-away defects typically stem from transmission or parking brake system failures and have triggered numerous high-profile recalls across the auto industry in recent years. The broad model year range and large number of affected vehicles suggest a systemic manufacturing or design issue rather than an isolated problem. Mercedes-Benz has not disclosed specific details about the root cause or whether customer incidents have been reported. Such safety defects in parking systems have become increasingly common as vehicles incorporate more complex electronic brake and transmission controls.

The 2027 timeline aligns with Audi's broader strategy to refresh its SUV lineup while transitioning toward electrified powertrains. The SQ9 will likely feature hybrid or electric performance technology to meet evolving emissions standards. This generation of performance SUVs represents an ongoing industry trend where manufacturers prioritize sportiness in larger, family-oriented vehicles.

title: BMW i4 Convertible Spotted with Soft Top and Neue Klasse Styling
summary: BMW's upcoming electric 4-series convertible was spotted testing, and despite camouflage, there's plenty to see.
whatHappening: BMW's electric 4-series convertible is undergoing real-world testing, with spy photos revealing a soft-top design and styling cues from the upcoming Neue Klasse platform. Despite heavy camouflage, the vehicle's convertible architecture and electric underpinnings are becoming visible to keen observers.
whoInvolved: BMW, the German luxury automaker, is developing this new model as part of its electrification strategy. The company has been aggressively expanding its i-branded EV lineup while preparing to launch its next-generation Neue Klasse platform.
whyMatters: This convertible represents BMW's commitment to offering electric alternatives across its entire model portfolio, capturing the premium EV convertible market that currently has limited options. The vehicle's development signals BMW's confidence in EV demand for lifestyle vehicles and could influence competitor strategies in the luxury convertible segment.
moreContext: BMW's 4-series convertible has been a key lifestyle offering in its lineup, and the shift to electric power reflects broader industry trends toward EV diversification beyond sedans and SUVs. The Neue Klasse platform, debuting with upcoming models, represents BMW's modernized EV architecture designed for improved efficiency and range. The soft-top design choice aligns with BMW's convertible heritage while potentially offering weight savings compared to traditional hard-tops, a consideration for EV range optimization. This testing phase typically precedes a launch within 12-24 months.

title: 2026 Honda CR-V EX-L vs. 2026 Mazda CX-5 Premium Plus Comparison Test
summary: The CX-5 and CR-V are both longtime Car and Driver favorites, but with the Mazda fully redesigned for 2026, which one comes out on top?
whatHappening: Car and Driver is pitting the 2026 Honda CR-V EX-L against the fully redesigned 2026 Mazda CX-5 Premium Plus to determine which compact crossover SUV reigns supreme. Both vehicles are established favorites at the publication, but Mazda's ground-up redesign reshuffles the competitive landscape.
whoInvolved: Honda and Mazda, two major Japanese automakers, are competing in the highly competitive compact crossover segment. Both companies have built strong reputations for reliability and driving dynamics, with their CR-V and CX-5 models consistently ranking among the segment's best-sellers.
whyMatters: Compact crossovers are the fastest-growing segment in the U.S. auto market, making this comparison critical for millions of shoppers deciding between two top contenders. The outcome could influence purchase decisions worth tens of billions in combined sales, as these vehicles represent some of the most popular models on American roads.
moreContext: The Honda CR-V has dominated its class for decades, known for spacious interiors and reliability. Mazda has spent years positioning the CX-5 as a more engaging, upscale alternative that prioritizes driving dynamics and design refinement. The 2026 CX-5 redesign marks a significant refresh, introducing new styling, updated technology, and potentially improved performance that could challenge the CR-V's market dominance. This comparison test arrives at a pivotal moment when shoppers can evaluate whether Mazda's redesign efforts successfully close the gap or establish a new benchmark in the segment.

title: View Photos of the 2027 Mercedes-Benz C-Class EV
summary: See the interior and exterior of the 2027 Mercedes-Benz C-class EV from every angle.
whatHappening: Mercedes-Benz is unveiling the 2027 C-Class EV with detailed photos showing both interior and exterior designs. The automaker is giving consumers a comprehensive first look at the electric version of its popular compact luxury sedan from multiple angles.
whoInvolved: Mercedes-Benz, the German luxury automaker, is behind this reveal. The company is one of the world's largest premium vehicle manufacturers and a major player in the global shift toward electrification.
whyMatters: This launch signals Mercedes-Benz's commitment to electrifying its core lineup, including mass-market luxury models. The 2027 C-Class EV could significantly influence the competitive landscape in the premium EV segment as traditional luxury brands compete with Tesla and newer EV manufacturers.
moreContext: Mercedes-Benz has aggressively pushed toward electrification, with plans to transition its entire lineup to electric vehicles by 2030 in developed markets. The C-Class is the automaker's best-selling model globally, making its EV variant crucial to the company's decarbonization strategy. This move comes as legacy automakers race to match Tesla's market dominance and meet tightening European emissions regulations. The 2027 timeline indicates the vehicle will arrive during a critical period when EV adoption is expected to accelerate significantly in luxury segments.

title: 2027 Mercedes-Benz C-Class EV Drive: EQ Who?
summary: The brand's latest electric sedan is way easier to like than its earlier efforts.
whatHappening: Mercedes-Benz is unveiling its 2027 C-Class EV, an electric sedan that marks a significant improvement over the brand's previous electric vehicle attempts. The new model is generating positive reception for its design and usability compared to earlier EQ offerings.
whoInvolved: Mercedes-Benz, the German luxury automaker, is pushing deeper into the electric vehicle market with this redesigned C-Class sedan. The company has been developing its EQ sub-brand for electric vehicles over the past several years.
whyMatters: This represents a critical moment for Mercedes' EV transition, as previous electric models faced criticism that could have damaged the brand's luxury reputation. A more compelling C-Class EV could accelerate adoption among luxury buyers and strengthen Mercedes' competitive position against Tesla and other EV manufacturers.
moreContext: Mercedes launched its EQ brand in 2016 but faced mixed reviews on early models that struggled with design appeal and user experience compared to the company's traditional combustion engine vehicles. The 2027 C-Class EV appears to address these shortcomings with improved aesthetics and functionality. The timing matters as luxury automakers face increasing pressure to electrify their core lineups to meet regulatory requirements and changing consumer preferences. Car and Driver's positive assessment suggests Mercedes may finally be cracking the code on making electric luxury sedans that satisfy both enthusiasts and practical buyers.

title: Land Rover Discontinues the Discovery Sport After 11 Years
summary: The Discovery Sport will end production in December, with 2026 becoming the compact SUV's final model year.
whatHappening: Land Rover is discontinuing the Discovery Sport, its compact SUV that has been in production for 11 years. Production will end in December, with 2026 being the final model year.
whoInvolved: Land Rover, the British luxury automaker owned by Jaguar Land Rover (a subsidiary of Tata Motors), is making this decision. The Discovery Sport has been a key model in their lineup since its 2014 debut.
whyMatters: The discontinuation reflects shifting market demands toward electric vehicles and larger SUVs, forcing traditional automakers to streamline their lineups. For buyers, this signals fewer options in the compact luxury SUV segment and may drive demand toward remaining competitors or push consumers toward Land Rover's other models.
moreContext: The Discovery Sport launched in 2014 as a replacement for the Freelander, becoming one of Land Rover's best-selling models globally. The move aligns with parent company Jaguar Land Rover's broader electrification strategy, as the company transitions toward battery-powered vehicles. This discontinuation comes as the automotive industry faces pressure to reduce internal combustion engine offerings. Land Rover continues to offer the larger Discovery and the Range Rover Sport, which may cannibalize some Discovery Sport sales.

title: Honda Could Target Subaru Outback Buyers with a Lifted Accord SUV
summary: Honda hopes that in the wake of the Outback's transformation into a more traditional SUV, buyers will flock to a reimagination of the Accord Crosstour.
whatHappening: Honda is considering reviving the Accord Crosstour as a lifted SUV to compete in the segment Subaru's Outback once dominated. The automaker sees an opportunity to capture buyers who are dissatisfied with the Outback's shift toward a more traditional SUV design.
whoInvolved: Honda, the Japanese automaker known for sedans and crossovers, is looking to capitalize on Subaru's strategic pivot. Subaru, maker of the Outback wagon-SUV hybrid, recently redesigned the model as a more conventional SUV, potentially alienating buyers who preferred its car-based platform.
whyMatters: A new Accord Crosstour could fill a niche gap for buyers seeking a vehicle with car-like handling and efficiency but with added ground clearance and cargo space. This move could help Honda attract Outback customers and strengthen its position in the crossover segment, which continues to grow.
moreContext: The original Accord Crosstour, produced from 2010 to 2015, was Honda's attempt at a lifted wagon but faced lukewarm sales due to uncertain positioning. Subaru's Outback has traditionally appealed to buyers wanting practicality without committing to a fully rugged SUV. The crossover market has exploded in recent years, with manufacturers increasingly creating variations to capture different buyer preferences. If Honda moves forward, it would represent a bet that there's still demand for car-based, efficiency-focused alternatives to traditional SUVs.

title: View Photos of the 2001 Qvale Mangusta
summary: See the interior and exterior of the 2001 Qvale Mangusta from every angle.
whatHappening: Car and Driver is showcasing a comprehensive photo gallery of the 2001 Qvale Mangusta, featuring detailed views of both the car's interior and exterior from multiple angles.
whoInvolved: Qvale Automotive Group, a San Diego-based manufacturer, produced the Mangusta as an Italian-designed, American-built sports car. Car and Driver, a leading automotive publication, is providing visual documentation of the vehicle.
whyMatters: The Qvale Mangusta represents a rare attempt at domestic supercar production during the early 2000s, offering insight into an ambitious but ultimately short-lived American sports car project. Visual walkarounds help enthusiasts and collectors understand the car's design details and engineering during a niche era of automotive manufacturing.
moreContext: The Qvale Mangusta was designed by Italian coachbuilder Qvale with a mid-mounted engine and carbon-fiber body, marking one of few American-made supercars of its generation. Only 12 examples were built before the company ceased operations in 2003, making it an obscure collectible. The car featured a 5.7-liter V8 engine and a sleek, aggressive design that drew influence from Italian sports car traditions. Its rarity and distinctive styling have made it a curiosity piece in automotive history.

title: AEV's Second Ford Super Duty Package Is Extreme Off-Road Lite
summary: Following the FXL revealed earlier this year, the FX370 makes do with 37-inch tires instead of 40s.
whatHappening: AEV has launched the FX370, its second extreme off-road Ford Super Duty package following the FXL introduced earlier this year. The new variant uses 37-inch tires instead of the FXL's 40-inch tires, offering a more accessible performance tier.
whoInvolved: AEV (American Expedition Vehicles) is a specialized manufacturer known for building high-performance off-road vehicle packages and upgrades. Ford Super Duty is the company's heavy-duty truck line targeting commercial and personal use.
whyMatters: The FX370 expands AEV's off-road truck portfolio to capture buyers seeking extreme capability without the maximum investment of the 40-inch tire setup. This tiered approach allows AEV to reach a broader market segment while maintaining premium positioning in the off-road truck segment.
moreContext: AEV has built a reputation for engineering rugged, expedition-ready truck packages that appeal to serious off-road enthusiasts and overlanding communities. The FXL's debut earlier this year marked AEV's aggressive push into the Ford Super Duty market. The 37-inch tire size represents a middle ground between standard Super Duty setups and extreme off-road builds, offering improved ground clearance and terrain capability while maintaining better highway manners and fuel efficiency than larger tires. This multi-tier strategy reflects growing consumer demand for customizable off-road vehicles.

title: Test: 2001 Qvale Mangusta Is a Head-Turner and a Head-Scratcher
summary: Owners will have some explaining to do.
whatHappening: Car and Driver is testing the 2001 Qvale Mangusta, a rare Italian-American sports car that turns heads but leaves owners scrambling for explanations. The vehicle is visually striking yet mechanically puzzling.
whoInvolved: Qvale Automobili, an Italian company, partnered with American engineering to produce the Mangusta. Car and Driver, a leading automotive publication, conducted the evaluation.
whyMatters: The Mangusta represents an unusual chapter in sports car history—a low-volume exotic that struggled to find its identity. Understanding vehicles like this reveals how ambitious automotive startups often fail to deliver on their promises despite appealing designs.
moreContext: The Qvale Mangusta was produced from 1998 to 2002 with extremely limited numbers, making it a rare curiosity today. The car attempted to blend Italian sports car aesthetics with American V8 power and practicality, but faced significant quality and reliability issues. Its obscurity means most enthusiasts have never heard of it, let alone seen one. The model exemplifies the risks of small independent manufacturers trying to compete against established luxury and performance brands.

title: Obsessively Maintained 1990 Ferrari Testarossa For Sale on BaT
summary: While another Testarossa with lower miles than this car's 3700 may exist, it's hard to imagine there's one that has been better cared for.
whatHappening: A pristine 1990 Ferrari Testarossa with only 3,700 miles is being offered for sale on Bring a Trailer (BaT), an online auction platform for collectible vehicles. The car has been obsessively maintained throughout its ownership history, setting it apart from other examples of the same model.
whoInvolved: Car and Driver is reporting on the sale, while Bring a Trailer (BaT) is the auction platform facilitating the transaction. BaT has become a major marketplace for high-end collector cars and enthusiasts seeking rare, well-documented vehicles.
whyMatters: Extremely low-mileage, meticulously maintained supercars command premium prices in the collector car market and represent investments for wealthy enthusiasts. The condition of this particular Testarossa—likely better preserved than competing examples—could set valuation benchmarks for 1990 models and influence future asking prices.
moreContext: The Ferrari Testarossa, produced from 1984 to 1996, is one of the most iconic supercars of the 1980s and early 1990s, known for its distinctive side strakes and 12-cylinder engine. Ultra-low-mileage, garage-kept examples are highly sought after by collectors because most Testarossas from this era have been driven substantially. The condition of a vehicle becomes exponentially more valuable as mileage decreases, with sub-5,000-mile examples commanding significant premiums over higher-mileage counterparts.

title: The Best Odds: 2000-01 Qvale Mangusta
summary: The cars I recall most fondly were neither the prettiest nor the quickest. Certainly not the most expensive. They were machines that emerged willfully peculiar and intractably idiosyncratic.
whatHappening: Car and Driver is reflecting on the 2000-01 Qvale Mangusta, celebrating it as a memorable automotive oddity rather than a conventional performance machine. The piece emphasizes how certain cars stand out not for being the fastest or most beautiful, but for their willfully peculiar and idiosyncratic character.
whoInvolved: Qvale Automobiles, a niche Italian-American sports car manufacturer, produced the Mangusta during the early 2000s. The company was known for creating small-batch, unconventional vehicles that prioritized distinctive character over mainstream appeal.
whyMatters: This perspective shift—valuing quirky authenticity over raw performance metrics—reflects a growing automotive enthusiasm for uniqueness and personality in an era increasingly dominated by mass-produced standardization. Such vehicles often become collector's items and cultural touchstones, influencing how enthusiasts evaluate automotive merit beyond horsepower and aesthetics.
moreContext: The Qvale Mangusta emerged during a period when independent sports car manufacturers competed fiercely against established brands by offering bold, unconventional designs. Rather than chasing top speed records or luxury price points, the Mangusta carved out identity through its distinctive styling and rare availability. This era of automotive history celebrated mechanical personality and driving experience, qualities that have experienced renewed appreciation among modern collectors and enthusiasts seeking alternatives to cookie-cutter modern vehicles.
